extracted.intended_audience: researchers, technologists, and organizations (academia, industry, government labs) considering or preparing R&D proposals to DARPA's Microsystems Technology Office (MTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for aligning research ideas and proposals to the Microsystems Technology Office priorities: seek transformational microsystems advances, demonstrate scalability/manufacturability, and show potential for dual-use transition. Encourages early engagement with MTO program managers and framing work around the office's thrust areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformational impact (not incremental)
rubrics_metrics.description: Go beyond incremental improvements to existing technologies and seek fundamental scientific breakthroughs that can create new capabilities and reshape entire industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MTO 'pushes today’s boundaries in foundational science to create transformational impact for tomorrow.' The office emphasizes revolutionary advances versus evolutionary capabilities; proposals should articulate how work is not merely an incremental improvement but could enable new capabilities or industry-scale change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Circuit Development thrust — Photonic Circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should advance photonic circuits by expanding the use of photonic interconnects, examining new materials and wavelengths, and designing new architectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals targeting photonics should address one or more of: novel photonic interconnect approaches at chip-scale, new material/wavelength solutions, or architectural designs that leverage light for improved microsystem performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Circuit Development thrust — Quantum Circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should explore quantum phenomena for computing and sensing, with attention to nearer-term and longer-term instantiations that reduce the possibility of commercial surprise, drive discovery of new hardware metrics, and invent scalable devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clarify temporal scope (near- vs long-term), identify new hardware metrics to be developed/validated, and demonstrate a path toward scalable quantum devices or sensing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Circuit Development thrust — Organic Circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation into biological and organic systems for computation and sensing, enabling integration of biomolecules and micro-technologies, establishing viability of molecular integrated circuits, and exploring hybrid bio-sensing and bio-compute microsystems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should show how biomolecular components can be integrated with microsystems, demonstrate viability or pathways to viability for molecular-scale circuits, and explore hybrid approaches combining biological and inorganic modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microsystems manufacturing ecosystem and manufacturability
rubrics_metrics.description: Build the infrastructure and tools necessary for producing and improving advanced microsystems, including exploring new additive, subtractive, and combination fabrication tools and technologies to enable sustainable manufacturing and speed time to market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address manufacturability, sustainable fabrication approaches, and methods to accelerate time-to-market. Emphasis on foundational ecosystem enhancements that extend beyond a single circuit technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use by design and transition potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop technologies with both military and commercial applications, focusing on innovations that strengthen national security while also enhancing the U.S. economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate both defense-relevant capabilities and commercial relevance, include strategies to leverage commercial scaling, and describe transition pathways (e.g., potential transition partners, commercialization plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design, integration, and hardware security
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore new capabilities in design and integration while addressing hardware security so systems can take advantage of commercial scaling yet retain defense differentiators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should consider secure design principles, integration approaches that enable robust operation in contested environments, and ways to retain or create differentiating capabilities for defense applications even when leveraging commercial ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and ability to scale for manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that technologies can be scaled for manufacture and practical deployment (e.g., 'Can these technologies scale for manufacture?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence, models, or plans showing how the proposed approach scales (fabrication throughput, cost, reliability) and how scaling challenges will be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on foundational science that enables new capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Push foundational scientific understanding that underpins future microsystem capabilities rather than only immediate engineering tweaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly separate foundational scientific objectives from incremental engineering work and explain how foundational advances lead to new device/system capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-driven framing: articulate challenges, opportunities, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas and proposals should state the scientific/technical challenge, the opportunities and limitations of approaches, and possible methods or architectures to address them (as in the 'Ideas Under Incubation' prompts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing an idea, enumerate the challenges, potential approaches, expected limitations, and the impact if successful. Example prompts on the page ('Can we improve...?', 'What are the challenges, opportunities, and limitations?') model this framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of timeline and market dynamics to reduce commercial surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially for quantum and other fast-moving fields, consider nearer-term and longer-term instantiations to reduce the possibility of commercial surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should show awareness of technology and market trends, articulate where the work sits on a near- to long-term timeline, and justify how that positioning mitigates risk of being overtaken by commercial developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with program managers and potential transition partners
rubrics_metrics.description: MTO program managers expect two-way engagement: talking to experts, potential transition partners, and each other during idea incubation and program development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective contributors should contact relevant PMs (contact info provided) early to discuss ideas, identify missing information, and explore transition opportunities; the 'Ideas Under Incubation' section explicitly invites such input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite program duration but lasting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that MTO programs are finite in duration, but should be designed to produce revolutionary advancements that create lasting change beyond the program lifecycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should define durable outcomes, transition plans, or ecosystem impacts that persist after program completion rather than only short-term demonstrations.
